sourceNote.title: Invoice PDF export
sourceNote.html:
Invoice PDF export

Testing the Export PDF action on the invoice detail page of a demo accounting app.

  • Invoice states: draft, sent, paid, cancelled. Only sent and paid invoices can be exported; draft and cancelled show the button disabled with a tooltip.

  • The PDF contains company logo, invoice number, dates, line items, VAT per rate (0%, 9%, 21%) and totals.

  • Invoices with more than 25 line items continue on a second page with the header repeated.

  • File name is invoice-<number>.pdf.

  • Observed: an invoice with a customer name containing "Müller & Söhne" exported fine, but the ampersand looked escaped in the file name preview.

  • Observed: export of a 60-line invoice took about 8 seconds with no progress indicator.

bodyHtml:
Feature: Invoice PDF export

Technique note: The note lists the invoice states (draft, sent, paid, cancelled) and the states in which export is allowed. It does not describe the events that move an invoice from one state to another, such as sending, paying or cancelling. These scenarios therefore treat each state as a precondition and check how the Export PDF action behaves in it. They do not test the transitions between states.

Scenario: Export availability by invoice state

Test case: Export is enabled for sent and paid invoices

Purpose: Confirm that Export PDF can be used in the two states where export is allowed.

Preconditions: The demo accounting app has one invoice in the sent state and one in the paid state.

Test data: Invoice A has the status sent. Invoice B has the status paid.

  • Given invoice A (sent) is open on the invoice detail page

  • When the user clicks Export PDF

  • Then a PDF is generated and downloaded

  • Repeat the steps for invoice B (paid)

Expected result: Export PDF is enabled for both invoices, and each export produces a PDF.

Coverage notes: This covers the valid path from sent or paid to an exported PDF.

Test case: Export is blocked for draft and cancelled invoices

Purpose: Confirm that export is not possible in the draft and cancelled states.

Preconditions: The demo accounting app has one invoice in the draft state and one in the cancelled state.

Test data: Invoice C has the status draft. Invoice D has the status cancelled.

  • Given invoice C (draft) is open on the invoice detail page

  • When the user hovers over the Export PDF button

  • Then the button is disabled and a tooltip is shown

  • When the user tries to click the disabled button

  • Then no PDF is generated

  • Repeat the steps for invoice D (cancelled)

Expected result: Export PDF is disabled and shows a tooltip for draft and cancelled invoices, and neither invoice can be exported.

Coverage notes: This is the negative case for the blocked states. The note does not give the tooltip text, so the tester should record the wording that appears.

Scenario: PDF content and layout

Test case: The PDF contains all required sections and the VAT breakdown

Purpose: Check that the exported PDF contains every section listed in the note and shows VAT for each rate.

Preconditions: There is a sent or paid invoice with line items at all three VAT rates.

Test data: One invoice with at least one line item at 0%, one at 9% and one at 21% VAT.

  • Given the invoice is open on the invoice detail page

  • When the user exports it as a PDF

  • Then the PDF shows the company logo, invoice number, dates and line items

  • And it shows separate VAT amounts for 0%, 9% and 21%

  • And it shows the totals

Expected result: All listed sections are present, and VAT is broken down per rate.

Test case: Page break after 25 line items (boundary)

Purpose: Check the boundary at which the PDF continues on a second page with the header repeated.

Preconditions: There are sent or paid invoices with the line-item counts listed below.

Test data: Invoices with 25, 26 and 60 line items.

  • Given the 25-line invoice is open

  • When the user exports it as a PDF

  • Then all line items fit on one page

  • Given the 26-line invoice is open

  • When the user exports it as a PDF

  • Then the line items continue on a second page and the header is repeated there

  • Given the 60-line invoice is open

  • When the user exports it as a PDF

  • Then the header is repeated on every continuation page, and the tester records the export time and whether any progress feedback appears

Expected result: Invoices with more than 25 line items continue on a second page with the header repeated.

Coverage notes: Earlier observation: exporting a 60-line invoice took about 8 seconds and showed no progress indicator. The note does not state an expected time or what progress feedback should look like, so record what you see.

Scenario: Export file naming

Test case: File name pattern with special characters in the customer name

Purpose: Check that the file name follows invoice-<number>.pdf, including for a customer name with special characters.

Preconditions: There is a sent or paid invoice for a customer named "Müller & Söhne".

Test data: Customer name "Müller & Söhne" and the invoice number of that invoice.

  • Given the invoice for "Müller & Söhne" is open on the invoice detail page

  • When the user exports it as a PDF

  • Then the file name preview and the downloaded file are named invoice-<number>.pdf

  • And the file name preview shows no escaped characters, such as an escaped ampersand

  • And the customer name inside the PDF shows "Müller & Söhne" correctly

Expected result: The file is named invoice-<number>.pdf, and special characters are displayed correctly.

Coverage notes: Earlier observation: the export worked, but the ampersand looked escaped in the file name preview. The note does not say whether the customer name should appear in the file name.
